content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm seeking advice. I have a [product_name] unit operating at 12/24V and have been utilizing its analog input features. I've noticed that when input voltage drops below approximately 0.3V, the readings become erratic. I discovered this while using LM35 sensors as well as with a voltage signal generator, which provides stable results until the voltage falls below 0.3V. Is the [product_name] capable of accurately reading millivolt-level signals?

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. The analog inputs of the [product_name] basic module have a fault tolerance of about 1.5%, meaning values within ±0.15V can be considered as error. Given a measurement range of 0.0 to 10.0V, the error in the area around 0.3V is significant. Temperature sensors such as the LM35 aren't suitable if precise measurements are required.
This issue was resolved in units manufactured after August 2019.
Which issue are you referring to?
The unit I'm using was made in November 2018 and has firmware version [version_no]. Measurement of millivolt signals seems fine at higher voltages, but not at the low end of the scale.

Thanks for sharing the link. Sadly, the update did not improve input performance. Above 0.3V, the input reads accurately in increments of 0.01V, but below this threshold, it fails to provide precise readings, which is disappointing.

That wasn't the main reason for recommending the update. The error at the lower end of the 0-10V range is much more pronounced. Therefore, my point stands: sensors like the LM35 aren't suitable for precise measurements with the [product_name] if accuracy is important.
I tried it mostly out of curiosity. I've stopped using the LM35 and tested with simple voltage instead. Thanks for your support; I appreciate it.
Hello [user_name], I'm unsure what [user_name] meant with their comment.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered unstable analog input readings from their [product_name] when measuring low voltage signals (below 0.3V). The device's significant fault tolerance at lower voltages results in inaccuracy for millivolt-level measurements. Firmware updates did not improve this limitation, which left the user dissatisfied with performance in low voltage applications.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that their [product_name]'s analog inputs will deliver reliable and precise measurements at low voltages, particularly below 0.3V and in the millivolt range.
